data.narrative:
The Lumber Manufactory is a Series C-stage robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $53.1M to date. Valuation analysis draws from a comparable universe of seven private companies at same or adjacent stages (Exotec, Generalist AI, Bedrock Robotics, Dexterity, and Hadrian among them), alongside one public comparable, offering a mixed-maturity peer set across the robotics and manufacturing sector.

Two methods triangulate valuation. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C-to-next-stage advancement to the $53M raised proxy, yielding $90M. Peer-median methodology anchors to the $1.6B median valuation across the seven-company comparable set, with observed range of $1.0B to $2.0B. The peer-median method carries greater weight given direct stage and sector alignment.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $77M (floor, driven by stage-progression) to $1.9B (ceiling, upper quartile of peer set), with a median of $870M. This wide band reflects material uncertainty around execution risk, competitive positioning within the robotics stack, and near-term revenue trajectory relative to peers. The stage-progression method may undervalue given sector dynamics, while peer-median carries concentration risk to private market sentiment in robotics. Key unknowns include revenue scale, gross margins, and customer concentration relative to the comparison set.
